lxc_15158267dcc53569.text: Then we practise keeping a conversation going with new people.

lxc_4f8ec52453853599.text: We learn how the evening works, how to order and how to introduce yourself.

lxc_d555e311d6c4cb5d.text: Today we visit a language exchange in a café.

lxc_d9071b9d11c7dcf7.text: When you arrive, you tell the host: I'm here for the language exchange.

lxc_be5cc778c0dc7347.text: People see your sticker, but they often ask too: Which languages do you speak?

lxc_4c29655e0792ab35.text: You answer: My native language is Japanese.

lxc_111249c0cb337d90.text: In this lesson, you visit the Dutch Language Café in The Hague.

lxc_624eca822556d2fd.text: A language exchange is a trade: you give something, and you get something.

lxc_86bf385310b2dbe1.text: On Thursday evenings, its language exchange starts at 19:30.

lxc_66700cb8fb4d68f6.text: The flag of your native language goes at the top.

lxc_1fa6a0fccbe790c1.text: Your native language is the first language you learned as a child.

lxc_4cd9574f58e9518c.text: Then you look for an English speaker who wants to practise Japanese.

lxc_7d9b92c3cab379ae.text: The Hague is a city in the Netherlands.

lxc_5e462c58db1269fb.text: Later, everyone sits at language tables, for example an English table.

lxc_5f29fc14600de601.text: You talk in one language for half an hour.

lxc_5e5f673f5b2b50bc.text: Then you talk in the other language for half an hour.

lxc_0e98d367e8a40cbb.text: For example, you speak Japanese and want to practise English.

lxc_8bf08219e5843807.text: At Mundo Lingo, a free language event, people put flag stickers on their shirts.

lxc_13783c369ce60ae6.text: The flags of the languages you study go below it.

lxc_56fc26d8752dbb49.text: Other people look at your flags and know your languages at once.

lxc_d4da58082390f65f.text: Then you get a sticker and write your languages on it.

lxc_68e89165ba8c7755.text: You help someone with your language, and they help you with theirs.

lxc_4fad4e0dae3ceb20.text: Many language cafés split the time in half.

lxc_43c0292e205f5698.text: This way, both people get the same time to learn.

lxc_37b553760650a724.text: This way, you meet many people quickly.

lxc_bc6005d7c599fb17.text: You talk with one person for 3 minutes.

lxc_259168d46713336c.text: But how do you find the right person in a busy room?

lxc_7a371213215dd8dc.text: Then you move to the next person.

lxc_f45418020331c7d2.text: You ask the host: Are the snacks included?

lxc_a448504af92a9ffc.text: Koffie verkeerd has more milk than coffee, so it is the wrong way around.

lxc_8b460c7f4893b7ab.text: If you are hungry, you ask the waiter: What is an empanada?

lxc_d3e78d2ea5cdd388.text: At the Dutch Language Café, the Thursday ticket costs €11.

lxc_077c516629f8ce2d.text: But a drink is a nice way to give something back.

lxc_be5f0dd4d441526f.text: A language exchange is free or cheap.

lxc_1acff9a0d71f0814.text: On the menu, you see a funny name: koffie verkeerd.

lxc_a1e2766359b51132.text: In English, koffie verkeerd is wrong coffee.

lxc_a9fa90fda71b91a0.text: At the bar, you order: Can I have a koffie verkeerd, please?

lxc_a110e0a9f0b16f83.text: Then you ask: How much is it?

lxc_e357cbabf338ebcd.text: At Mundo Lingo, you do not have to buy anything.

lxc_bf36a4f767ef8d47.text: So people buy a drink to say thank you.

lxc_87d88bb2ee8f0e57.text: But the café gives you the room, the tables and the chairs all evening.

lxc_3a0a45d9c1f9f77c.text: It is a small pastry, with cheese, meat or vegetables inside.

lxc_105618402da7ee4c.text: It includes, or gives you, free snacks and games.

lxc_7b81f376a272e854.text: A normal Dutch coffee has only a little milk.

lxc_a46986069769153a.text: But drinks are not in the ticket, so you buy them at the bar.

lxc_28ef28df1dc5ce5c.text: Then you say: Nice to meet you.

lxc_eb73c8843a1754ae.text: At the same time, they say their name: Hi!

lxc_eb9d27b5c26e4003.text: Then Lucía asks: What about you?

lxc_37a2b694e0255af4.text: In the Netherlands, people shake hands when they meet someone new.

lxc_0e9268a92cb6d9db.text: In a 3-minute speed exchange, you do not have much time.

lxc_30b2221e2f75d01f.text: the first time you meet a Dutch person.

lxc_94f247c312aee428.text: It gives people a question to ask, for example: Where do you work?

lxc_158c0f772b92554f.text: In Japan, many people bow, or bend forward, and say their family name.

lxc_8d13b3af654e3b7e.text: Often they say only their first name.

lxc_34c9c0d78ca28735.text: I study Dutch because I work in The Hague.

lxc_e53a0822309f0990.text: So say three things: your name, your city and why you study the language.

lxc_a662056fd15ba6ce.text: Many Dutch people use this question only with people they already know.

lxc_5522500b712d8f69.text: A stranger is a person you do not know.

lxc_7d7468ef8ea5c5a3.text: If a stranger asks this, a Dutch person may think you met before.

lxc_829977b9f83b6c04.text: But for Dutch people, a hello without a name is rude, or not polite.

lxc_79b676b369051b7c.text: Dutch people like to be clear, so they start with a name.

lxc_16ada43dd26b5b23.text: They may think they forgot you!

lxc_30bcfd3c5326ba65.text: The last part is the most useful.

lxc_af8ef6119f9d3b02.text: When you hear a new name, you say your name too.

lxc_ca9d5be49d18ee8c.text: You ask about time: How long have you lived here?

lxc_22f629be4dee748c.text: Mundo Lingo has a short rule: stand to mingle, sit to quit.

lxc_88cf2e04819f3fc3.text: Say: It was nice to talk to you.

lxc_9d42a6c14fcab8c0.text: You ask about her city: What is Valencia like?

lxc_8896722b0cdff6fe.text: Follow-up questions worked best of all.

lxc_f878fb0b77656db0.text: The best tool for a long conversation is the follow-up question.

lxc_8e49566cd88581e0.text: A follow-up question stays with her idea: What do you do at the hotel?

lxc_2fb285e280d65b22.text: Each follow-up question uses one part of what she says.

lxc_35e8758968283b24.text: A follow-up question shows that you are really listening.

lxc_4dc3f50d05ebb25f.text: In 2017, scientists at Harvard University studied how strangers talk.

lxc_a8969a66b0f25090.text: This is a question about what the other person just said.

lxc_d517d32670053e50.text: If you sit down, you are taking a break.

lxc_68a7dcdb9ffe0ae7.text: When you want to leave, end the conversation in a kind way.

lxc_cb9224fecd7050de.text: To mingle is to walk around and talk to many people.

lxc_63a75ea32b2df901.text: People who asked more questions were liked more by their partners.

lxc_b89e2620baadbb0e.text: A new question jumps to a new idea: Do you like football?

lxc_b3b637f84eb9fa27.text: Lucía also says: I moved here from Valencia.

lxc_102f1b31efebc9be.text: Your body tells people things too.

lxc_f6420a1a74c69985.text: If you stand, you are open to new people.

lxc_531732b196593552.text: You ask about her reason: Really?

lxc_f03616b1082c6c54.text: Lucía says: I work at a hotel.

lxc_e2c38dd53c315229.text: You arrive at the Dutch Language Café, Herengracht 13A, in The Hague.

lxc_c82dcb5afb6f2e4e.text: You signed up online, and your ticket was €11.

lxc_84e58c3f3d6dcbf5.text: Your goal: get your sticker, then order a drink and some food.

lxc_e3ce10d3517bed87.text: A host says hello to you.

lxc_894430d8dd088118.text: Your goal: shake hands, say your name and learn something about her.

lxc_dd63f65f637ed0a4.text: You sit down at a table with your coffee.

lxc_72883b9fe2ff3794.text: Her sticker shows Dutch, English and Spanish.

lxc_7dcde20e2b712b28.text: A Dutch woman sits next to you.

lxc_0b6d6975aac1ec22.text: You and your partner take turns choosing the language.

lxc_3a85720eb8487a90.text: Your goal: practise English first, then help Daan with his Japanese.

lxc_4ec9bfad3ffddaf4.text: His sticker shows Dutch, English and a little Japanese.

lxc_b0c6e8b1bd82d79e.text: You talk with each person for 3 minutes.

lxc_05e09dc2603eb6b8.text: Your goal: ask follow-up questions, then end the conversation in a kind way.

lxc_b085b1ad9a7f525a.text: It is 20:30, and you sit at the English table.

lxc_2b090369d7a0fbcc.text: Sanne is there, and you meet Lucía from Spain.

lxc_6c6c4c00a448205f.text: Ask at least three follow-up questions.

lxc_a1000f2c3e15a42f.text: Practise the evening at the Dutch Language Café again.

lxc_b8b6bcc635834630.text: The other person plays the host, the waiter, Sanne, Daan and Lucía.

lxc_b7703653687e77c5.text: Get your sticker, and order a koffie verkeerd and a cheese empanada for €10.50.

lxc_2284f4d089622ca9.text: Shake hands, and say your name, your city and why you study English.

lxc_2c9a49e5c5fa83d2.text: One of you is the visitor.

lxc_d78c8a65dce62ec1.text: Then change roles and use your real life.
